title: No vehicles in the park
intro: A by-law of 1958 says: no vehicles in the park. A later emergency rule lets a vehicle on an emergency call in, and a war memorial (an old tank on a plinth) was never meant to be caught. Switch on what arrives at the gate and watch which rules fire, which are defeated and why. This is H. L. A. Hart's famous example (1958): a rule has a clear core and a penumbra, and its exceptions are other rules that beat it.
emergencyLabel: It is on an emergency call
memorialLabel: A tank placed as a war memorial
ruleBicycleWord: In everyday speech a bicycle is a vehicle.
ruleBicycleDef: The by-law means motor vehicles only: a bicycle is not one.
ruleNoVehicles: No vehicles in the park (unless it is a memorial).
ruleEmergency: A vehicle on an emergency call may enter.
r1Label: The no-vehicles rule: 2 fires, 1 is defeated, 0 does not apply
sceneTitle: The rules and which beats which
checkDefeated: The no-vehicles rule applies but is defeated.
